newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Bodies litter countryside to west of Zaire camps.
newsitem.headline: Bodies litter countryside to west of Zaire camps.

text.p: Half a million refugees have gone home to Rwanda from east Zaire in the past few days but the bodies of others caught up in the fighting in the area litter the countryside to the west of the refugee camps.
This correspondent drove into the hills behind Sake but was blocked by Zairean rebels outside a small village and ordered to turn round.
In the bush at the side of the road were the bodies of at least three people.
Journalists who attempted to count the bodies were told they would have problems if they did not turn round and leave.

On a road that led from Sake towards the Masisi region, whose centre, Masisi town, is 90 kms (55 miles) due west of Sake, journalists discovered a mother, father and five children who had been killed with machetes, clubs and bullets.
A child strapped to its mother's back lay with its head entirely smashed open and its brains on the road.

Further on into the Masisi, another two bodies were discovered. These people had apparently been killed as refugees stampeded through the forest, fleeing the attack on the Mugunga camp by Zairean rebels.
That attack broke the stranglehold of the Rwandan Hutu extremists on the camp, allowing hundreds of thousands of the refugees finally to pluck up the courage to head home.
Some 1.1 million Hutus fled Rwanda in mid-1994 after the country was overrun by Tutsi rebels, now in government, after the genocide of up to a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus by Hutu extremists.
The entire area around Kirotshce, Minova and Sake to the west of Lake Kivu was controlled by large numbers of heavily-armed Zairean rebel troops, some of them no more than 10 years old.

Local people in the area told journalists that some 7,000 people from Bukavu camp who had tried to move northwards towards Goma last week had been blocked by Hutus belonging to the Interahamwe militia halfway along Lake Kivu.

Etienne Mahangaiko, medical director of Kirotshe hospital, 10 kms (five miles) north of Minova said that former Rwandan government forces came to Kiniezire, half way up lake Kivu and moved west to Numbi, some 30 to 40 kms (20 to 25 miles) into the Masisi region.
Behind them members of the Interahamwe were herding the 7,000 refugess towards Numbi.
"The Interahamwe wanted to go west with the refugees but Zairean rebels and Rwandan forces blocked the Masisi when the camp emptied," he said.
